source:
The small houses of wood and clay begin to block my view of the pines. 

My silent companion, the well, has long been dry and sealed. And yet, more people arrive and settle around us across these past few years. They dry clothes on my branches, gather my seed pods in the summer, pray in my shade, urinate on my trunk, mate under my darkness… They force me to be part of their life. I am named.   

Are the great pines ever bothered like this? Are they forced to gaze at little else than the humans and their irksome unpredictability? Their shortsightedness? Generations of wayward lives? 

Do the pines gaze back with jealousy? Do they yearn to be needed by humans? Valued beyond beams and firewood? Do the evergreens think they’d be happier with more respect from the great shapers of our world?

Stars have names. Great structures have names. Friends have names. The pines do not have names. 

I am named. 

I am named Great Nav’ed. 

I am apprehensive to hope, but I think this is good.

高大的松树，也受这样打扰吗？也被迫只能看人类，以及他们恼人的莫测、短视，一代代任性的生命吗？

松树会嫉妒地望回来吗？渴望被人需要吗？价值不只梁木与柴火？常青树会以为，获得世界塑造者更多尊重，就更快乐吗？

星辰有名字，宏伟建筑有名字，朋友有名字。松树没有。

我有名字。

我叫伟大的纳维德。

我不敢抱希望，但想，这很好。

source: Did You Know? Creating an Exomnus sentence is much like drawing a portrait of a person. First, you sketch the shape of the concept, like the face, and create boundaries. Then you section the material into understandable nuggets – eyes, ears, nose, expression. You keep information simple as you add it, then infuse precise detail like lighting and shadow. The process is similar with Exomnus. We first use words to create a simple idea. Then we take the Dictopedia, which holds all defined meanings of all words we know, and add precise references to the meanings we want each word to hold. The end result is a highly precise idea!
target: 你知道吗？ 造艾克索姆语句子，很像画人物肖像。先勾勒概念轮廓，如脸形，确立边界，再分成易懂的小块：眼、耳、鼻、表情。逐步加入简单资讯，再赋予精确细节，如光影。艾克索姆语也相似：先用词建立简单想法，再查收录所有已知词义的《辞义百科》，为每个词添上所需意思的精确参照。最后，便得到高度精确的想法！

source:
Pa, look – a daisy, I believe. Growing in the shade of your gravestone. “Nav’ed Praetis, Father of the Quentinites.” Father. Father…  

Everytime I come out to see you in our pines a deep envy heats my blood. I cannot help it. People knew you as Father longer than me. I never met the visionary mind who fathomed Exomnus. You never met the QUEEN OF QUENT, heh. The title makes me shudder. I — my journey never meant to be so long…

How peaceful, though. Our Quentinite Brothers and Sisters chose well to bury you in this clearing. Each time I visit there are more young shoots, greener needles, richer birdsong... our people truly are bringing the forest back to life from Rekter's destruction. 

I came by to tell you something incredible. Do you remember your ambitions with the roadrunners and the maps? Well, we are very close to finishing your work. The Great Waterhole Roads, a trade and travel system spanning in each direction from our city, will grow us into the Library of the World! 

As before, violent marauders find their way to our borders and cause bloodshed. But our forging and engineering knowledge combines to give us many missile weapons. Why, our crossbows make city defenders out of the old weavers! 

I will admit, I never imagined the complexity of settling a constant influx of migrants. How would you manage it, Pa? My best guess would be free but mandatory education as a path to Quent citizenship. But all the intricate customs, squabbles, beliefs, biases… how should law and justice accommodate these? Building society is the most frustrating work of my life. 

I worry my Ebned and Ravani may not be suited for the throne of Quent. Precocious and intelligent as my children are, it is Sadie Sloan who holds the most brilliant imagination for progress. 

We’re already exploring her theories on “printing” words for mass texts like a “news on paper” and using wind as a source of energy. And she dreams of greatness: harnessing electricity for night-time lights, exploding powder for defenses and mining, machines for sowing, currency for economy,  “typing” contraptions to assist our scribes.... All ideas from a place in her mind called Asbury. I tend to think she would have the most unique solutions to a growing society’s challenges. 

Ah, chill bumps. The night is bringing the cooled air. I will see you again soon, Pa.
target:
爸，看，一朵雏菊，大概是。长在你墓碑的荫下。「纳维德・普雷蒂斯，昆汀之父。」父亲。父亲……

每次来松林看你，深深的嫉妒就烧热血液。我忍不住。别人认识身为「父亲」的你，比我更久。我没见过构思艾克索姆语的远见头脑，你也没见过昆特女王，嘿。这头衔让我发抖。我……旅程本不该那么久……

可这里多平静。昆汀兄弟姊妹选这空地安葬你，选得好。每次都有更多幼苗、更绿松针、更丰富鸟鸣。族人确实在雷克特的破坏后，让森林重生。

今天来说件不可思议的事。记得走鹃与地图的志向吗？我们快完成你的工作了。大水源道，从城里向各方延伸的商旅系统，将使我们成为世界的图书馆！

和以前一样，暴力掠夺者找到边境，造成流血。但冶锻与工程知识结合，给了我们许多远射武器。弩竟能让年老织工也成为守城者！

我承认，从没想过安置不断涌入的移民这么复杂。爸，你会怎么办？我想最好是免费但强制的教育，作为取得昆特公民资格的途径。可习俗、争执、信仰、偏见，如此错综，法律与正义该如何容纳？建设社会，是我一生最挫折的工作。

我担心艾布内德和拉瓦妮不适合昆特王位。孩子虽早慧聪敏，对进步最有绝妙想像力的，却是莎蒂・斯隆。

我们已研究她「印刷」文字、大量制作「纸上新闻」的想法，以及用风作能源。她梦想伟大事物：电力夜灯、防卫采矿用爆炸粉末、播种机、经济货币、辅助抄写员的「打字」机关……全来自她心里一个叫阿斯伯里的地方。我总觉得，她能为成长社会的难题，提出最独特的解法。

啊，起鸡皮疙瘩了，夜带来凉意。爸，很快再来看你。
